evidence.section: The Dwarf Kingdoms / Humans Among Dwarfs
evidence.quote: fabulous arched spans that stretch between mountain peaks
evidence.claim: Named bridges are an explicit part of Dwarf infrastructure. This passage also names Barakdokerinnalad, Dalgrongi and Unzaled; reserve those identities. The age, dimensions and rumoured runes of those particular bridges are not generated properties.

evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Select the documented colour and object senses. These compounds are Forthammer compositions, not a claim that a complete bridge-naming grammar is available.

evidence.quote: Dok Watch, observe, see, the eye
evidence.claim: Bryn selects shiny/brilliant; dok selects the eye as a visual emblem. Neither grants supernatural sight, a watch service or a documented bridge decoration.
Gorl selects the colour sense rather than gold composition.
Kol selects black and skarrenruf selects bright blue; no sky location, bridge material or actual painted sign is implied.

evidence.quote: Zhuf Waterfall or rapidly flowing river
evidence.claim: Zhuf selects the flowing-river image; und is specifically a mountainside watchpost, and zan selects red rather than blood. Their use is symbolic, not invented geography or history.

evidence.section: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire Volume I / Of Karak Azgaraz / Unzaled Sky-Bridge and Migdhal Skarrenruf; Loremaster offset 233729
evidence.quote: The gatehouse of Mighdal Skarrenruf stands at the north end
evidence.claim: A named bridge with a guarded entry supplies context for watch and eye motifs; the printed Watchful Eagle Gate translation further grounds vigilance imagery. Choosing these images for a new bridge is an adaptation, not evidence of a real gatehouse or garrison. Reserve both Migdhal and Mighdal spellings printed in this section.

evidence.section: Of Karak Azgaraz / Unzaled Sky-Bridge and Migdhal Skarrenruf; Loremaster offset 232730
evidence.claim: Anvil imagery is printed in the translated name of an actual Dwarf bridge. The new names use independently attested Grong (anvil), do not infer plural morphology from Dalgrongi, and do not inherit the canonical bridge identity or age.

evidence.section: Of Karak Azgaraz / Unzaled Sky-Bridge and Migdhal Skarrenruf; Loremaster offset 232730
evidence.claim: Gate imagery is printed in a Dwarf bridge name. New labels use the independently attested Bar sense as a symbolic gate image, without asserting a gatehouse, owner, garrison or safe crossing.

evidence.section: p.44, Khazalid Glossary: Bar, Duraz, Azul
evidence.quote: Bar A fortified gateway or door
evidence.claim: Bar supplies a gate image. The same page supplies stone (Duraz) and metal of any kind (Azul) as materials of a proposed image, never the bridge construction material.

evidence.section: p.45, Khazalid Glossary: Grong and Galaz
evidence.claim: Anvil is the exact singular glossary sense. Galaz on the same page supplies gold of ornamental value for the image, not bridge construction or ownership of gold.

evidence.quote: Wutroth Wood from ancient mountain oak
evidence.claim: The symbolic oak gate preserves the full attested material sense. It does not promise an oak-built bridge or nearby ancient woods.
Silver and bread are attested independent concepts, not invented product or wealth claims.
The glossary distinguishes a musical horn from horn material, and attests road and thunder. Selected nouns remain literal word senses inside adapted labels.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

High-resolution printed text confirms Zunthrum with n. Spear, money, sunset, remembering and gift are independently attested; none assigns actual stock, wealth, a historical event or a commemorated person.
